The psh definition, reference reduction and field reduction are checked; rational approximation covers every ample real numerical class.
notes.detailedSummary: The body theorem covers geometrically unibranch varieties, beyond the normal-only introductory statement. Wu’s sequence-based global psh definition agrees with BJ’s for the trivial ample reference by model-nef criteria and unconditional countable regularization. A very ample multiple verifies the embedding-reference reduction actually needed. The countable case uses resolution, connected geometric fibers and Wu’s local-to-global regularization chain. Countability is removed using finite model data, genuine energy orthogonality, model-measure base change and BJ’s general-variety domination principle. Wu’s supplied preprint theorem is used as a mathematical source input; its unidentified APW bibliography is recorded without claiming independent verification.
notes.text:
Mathematical claim, using the supplied source theorems. Let k be algebraically closed, trivially valued and of characteristic zero, let X be reduced, irreducible, geometrically unibranch and projective, and let omega be an ample real numerical Cartier class. The usc regularization of a nonempty bounded-above family of genuine global BJ omega-psh functions is omega-psh. Equivalently, P_omega(f) is continuous for every continuous obstacle f. No countability assumption remains.

The exact new input is Wu, arXiv:2609.27610v1, body Theorem 7.1: “Let K be a discretely valued or trivially valued non-archimedean field of equicharacteristic 0 and X be a geometrically unibranch projective variety over K, then X satisfies the envelope property over K.” Its complete Section 7 proof is preserved at one-based inclusive LF lines 2696–2750. The introductory Theorem A is narrower; Theorem 6.5 initially assumes a countable dense subfield.

For an ample rational line bundle with trivial reference, BJ Lemma 4.3 identifies model psh functions with relatively nef classes. BJ Corollary 12.18 supplies decreasing sequences without assuming envelopes. Wu Definition 2.7 and Propositions 2.10–2.11 therefore give the same global cone: nef approximants can be approximated by ample models, with summable errors and decreasing tails of constants. For Theorem 6.5’s reference reduction, choose mL very ample and its complete-linear-system embedding. The trivial metric on mL is the pullback of the trivial projective-space metric; scaling back verifies the needed case. An arbitrary semipositive model reference is not simply identified with that embedding reference.

For countable k, resolve pi:Y→X. The class pi*omega is nef, so BJ Theorem 5.20 gives envelopes on smooth Y even though the pullback need not be ample. Geometric unibranchness gives connected geometric resolution fibers. Wu Proposition 2.24 descends the upstairs envelope and identifies its minimal usc extension from divisorial values. Divisorial nonnegligibility identifies it with the downstairs usc supremum. Wu Theorem 6.5 makes this weakly psh function globally psh. Its actual proof uses affine-chart potentials rho_j=max_l log|z_l|−log|z_j|: Theorem 6.3 regularizes phi+rho_j with logarithmic growth; Lemma 3.25 makes the extension of phi−(c−1)rho_j globally c omega-psh. Their maximum is phi because min_j rho_j=0; let c decrease to one. Theorem 6.3’s supplied proof uses singular-stratum induction, finite projections, norms, Runge arguments and distance regularization. Countability enters the strict supporting-function construction in Section 6.1.

For arbitrary cardinality, descend the finite model data of a PL obstacle to a countable algebraically closed k1⊂k. Geometric unibranchness descends: normalization remains normal under the regular field extension, and multiple geometric branches would persist. Set u1=P(f1). The envelope of u1+t(f1−u1) is u1 for 0≤t≤1. Genuine BJ energy differentiation gives integral(f1−u1) MA(u1)=0, hence contact support. A model psh competitor descends to a larger countable algebraically closed k2. The genuine model intersection formula, unchanged vertical multiplicities and unchanged intersection numbers give r21*MA(r21*u1)=MA(u1), extended by decreasing approximation. The competitor is at most r21*u1 almost everywhere for this measure. BJ Corollary 10.6 gives the inequality everywhere on the singular general variety; no smooth equation theorem is applied there. Supremizing model competitors proves P(f)=r_k1*P(f1). PL density covers continuous obstacles. Rational ample classes approaching omega from above and BJ Lemma 5.9 give all ample real classes.

Normality implies geometric unibranchness; connectedness or irreducibility alone does not supply the required geometric fiber condition. Wu Lemma 2.25’s displayed −m phi is replaced by the correct decreasing m phi for phi≤0.

Wu’s PDF SHA-256 is 11808a6c9ede9c0158b27e16700fc180a4ac8df12a4586a7178e1958e8f6bba8; its extract SHA-256 is c8ffe91a631da67f6d3872a1a06ab8d15755aed2f926cdf326725ca3662cef7d. Both match the supplied caches. Wu is a v1 preprint, used as an allowed source theorem without independent certification. APW26a/b have no identifiers in its bibliography; their separate texts were not supplied or read. The invoked local input is Wu’s supplied Theorem 6.3 and proof chain, not an independently verified APW theorem.

The complete argument is P16.1-argument.md; the standalone paper is P16.1-paper.tex. notes.summary: BJ v4 constructs the genuine mixed finite-energy intersection operator before smoothness, including nonnormal generic fibers. Energy uses (n+1)V, raw diagonal mass is V, and positivity, mixed integrability, model agreement and decreasing/strong continuity hold.
notes.detailedSummary: Relative integral closure preserves the given nonnormal generic fiber while providing vertical DVR valuations. The compactified model intersection pairing extends by decreasing approximation and then multilinearly to differences of finite-energy functions. Theorem 7.18 defines the mixed Radon measure through PL testing; Proposition 7.19 proves its exact model formula, mass, integrability and continuity. The construction is independent of solving equations. The normalized diagonal measure has mass one and E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c. Surjectivity requires the additional envelope input.
notes.text:
Mathematical construction from BJ1801.08229v4. Its ambient scope permits reduced singular and nonnormal projective varieties over an algebraically closed trivially valued field. Section 7 explicitly retains this general scope.

For nonnormal X, a test configuration is integrally closed in its given generic fiber: an affine k[t]-algebra A is closed in A⊗k(t). BJ Definition 1.10 and Theorem 1.13 give finite relative integral closure, unchanged generic X, and vertical R1/S2. Thus each generic vertical component E has a DVR, with b_E=ord_E(t) and v_E=b_E^(-1)ord_E restricted to k(X). Absolute normalization instead has generic fiber X^nu and cannot silently replace the model of X.

On a common configuration dominating the trivial one, phi_i=phi_Di. The model energy pairing is the intersection product of theta_i,barX+Di on its P1 compactification. Projection formula makes it independent of the dominating configuration. The genuine mixed model measure is
Σ_E b_E [product_i (theta_i,X+Di)|_E] delta_vE.
Its integral against a PL function h equals the pairing with first entry (0,h). Nefness makes the weights positive; flatness gives total mass (theta_1…theta_n)_X.

BJ Theorem 7.1 extends the pairing to psh tuples by infima over Hdom model majorants, with monotonicity, weak upper semicontinuity and decreasing-net continuity. Define V=(omega^n)>0 and E(phi)=pairing((omega,phi)^(n+1))/((n+1)V). Then E(0)=0 and E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c. E1 consists of psh potentials with finite real energy; it contains bounded psh functions, is convex and is upward closed within PSH. Theorem 7.8 proves finite mixed pairings for E1 functions in different ample classes by comparing classes and bounding the energy of their sum. Theorem 7.14 extends the pairing multilinearly to N1(X)×Etilde1, where Etilde1 consists of differences of finite-energy psh functions.

Theorem 7.18 defines the unique mixed signed Radon measure by
integral h M = pairing((0,h),(theta_1,phi_1),…,(theta_n,phi_n))
for h in PL_R. In the nef-psh case the functional is positive, has value (theta_1…theta_n)_X at 1, and is bounded by that mass times ||h||∞. PL density and Riesz representation construct the positive measure; multilinearity supplies the signed case. Proposition 7.19(ii) gives exactly the model atomic formula above. Consequently the operator agrees with genuine intersection measures on models and, by decreasing approximation, on all E1. It is not a convenient inverse measure construction.

The raw diagonal measure (omega+dd^c phi)^n has mass V; MA(phi)=V^(-1) times that measure has mass one. On irreducible X, MA(0)=delta_vtriv. Proposition 7.19(v) proves that finite-energy test functions are integrable against mixed finite-energy measures and preserves the pairing identity. Decreasing model approximants, mixed pairing finiteness and usc monotone convergence prove this integrability. Differences have unambiguous almost-everywhere representatives because positive mixed measures put no mass on pluripolar sets.

Proposition 7.19(iv) proves decreasing continuity by PL testing. Proposition 7.21 proves weighted decreasing continuity; the correct integral in its proof is the pairing with (omega0,phi0) minus the pairing with (omega0,0), correcting the reversed displayed sign. Theorem 7.34’s Hölder estimate proves strong continuity of mixed measures after normalizing suprema. These constructions do not require envelope surjectivity or smoothness.

BJ’s PDF SHA-256 is 8d5975337f4ac88a475929ea6a436ec4a15d08715d5582bc0ba0eb3e07152c52; its extract SHA-256 is 659bb8d2e5335781041f03cdb168bac70126487bc0db394f3dac8cf1e9f076d0. Theorem 7.18 and Proposition 7.19 are preserved with their actual general-variety proofs in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. Full reconstruction is in P16.1-argument.md and P16.1-paper.tex. Run python3 rerun.py. Hash verification is preservation evidence, not mathematical certification. Surjectivity is established separately in n3.

notes.summary: In the n1 domain, the n2 genuine operator solves exactly mass-V targets of finite dual energy, uniquely modulo one constant. General-variety compactness, differentiation, bounded-J integration, comparison and I-completeness replace the smooth inputs; Theorem 12.9’s smoothness is not imported into Theorem 12.8.
notes.detailedSummary: For mu=nu/V the exact condition is sup(E(psi)−integral psi mu)<∞, equivalent on irreducible X to integrability of every E1 potential. Strict energy concavity bounds J along normalized maximizing sequences. The envelope property gives genuine normalized psh compactness, and Proposition 9.19 supplies bounded-J L1 convergence against the fixed target, yielding attainment. Two-sided differentiation tests the genuine operator and proves that maximizers solve the equation. General-variety energy separation gives uniqueness and domination; model locality yields comparison. Target-space completeness and the bi-Lipschitz MA embedding give I-completeness after surjectivity.
notes.text:
Mathematical claim. In the retained domain of n1, using the genuine operator of n2, a positive Radon nu of raw mass V=(omega^n) is solvable by an E1 potential precisely when mu=nu/V satisfies
E_dual(mu)=sup_{psi in E1}(E(psi)−integral psi mu)<∞.
There is one additive real constant ambiguity on irreducible X; sup phi=0 fixes it. Finite-energy potentials may equal −∞ on pluripolar sets. Arbitrary measure support is permitted subject to the exact energy condition.

Necessity follows from mixed integrability and the tangent inequality:
E(psi)−integral psi MA(phi) ≤ E(phi)−integral phi MA(phi),
with equality at psi=phi. Thus a solution has finite dual energy. BJ Theorem 9.20 proves the converse characterization of the condition by all-E1 integrability. On normalized bounded-J sets, −integral psi mu is uniformly bounded, otherwise a sum Σ2^(−j)psi_j would have finite energy but integral −∞. The mixed expansion gives J(t psi)≤C_n t²J(psi), so rescaling gives −integral psi mu≤A sqrt(J(psi))+B. Subtracting J bounds the dual supremum. The raw variational supremum is V E_dual(nu/V).

Compactness replacement: BJ Theorem 5.11 uses n1’s envelopes to give compactness of the genuine normalized PSH space for divisorial pointwise convergence. Bounded divisorial evaluations give a Tychonoff subnet. Usc tail suprema are psh and decrease to its psh limit, because divisorial points are nonnegligible. This is not compactness on one skeleton.

Differentiation replacement: BJ Theorem 8.5 gives the uniform formula E_downarrow(phi+epsilon f)=E(phi)+epsilon integral f MA(phi)+O(epsilon²) for PL_R directions, on general projective varieties. Its proof uses determinant-of-cohomology volumes, auxiliary ample model differences, fixed mixed masses and decreasing approximation. Apply the formula to f and −f. Uniform approximation of continuous f gives |E_downarrow(phi+t f)−E_downarrow(phi+t f_m)|≤|t|eta_m; the correct derivative endpoints are integral f_m MA minus eta_m and plus eta_m. Under envelopes, Proposition 8.3 identifies E_downarrow with E(P(phi+t f)). This proves the required two-sided derivative for the actual operator.

Existence: write F_mu=E−integral phi mu and J_mu=E_dual−F_mu. Take a sup-zero maximizing sequence, which may be model-valued. Strict energy concavity measured by I gives J(phi_i)≤C_n(J_mu(phi_i)+E_dual), hence bounded J. Compactness gives a weakly convergent subnet phi_i→phi, and lower semicontinuity of J makes phi finite-energy. Proposition 9.19 is essential: weak psh convergence with eventually bounded J gives L1 convergence against the fixed finite-energy target, including unbounded potentials. Its proof approximates the target by genuine model MA measures with uniform bounded-J integration error. The correct absolute-value identity is |phi_i−phi|=2 max(phi_i,phi)−phi_i−phi. Thus the target integrals converge, and energy usc gives F_mu(phi)≥limsup F_mu(phi_i)=E_dual. The supremum is attained.

The maximizer-to-equation step tests the already constructed operator. For any maximizing net with deficit delta_i and epsilon>0, Legendre duality and uniform differentiation give
epsilon integral f (MA(phi_i)−mu) ≤ delta_i+C_f epsilon².
First pass to the net limit, then epsilon→0, and repeat with −f. PL density proves MA(phi_i)→mu. A constant maximizing net gives MA(phi)=mu. This also supplies the model approximation used in Proposition 9.19 without assuming attainment, avoiding circularity. Multiplication by V proves the raw equation.

Comparison and uniqueness: BJ Theorem 7.40 proves locality for maxima using vertical integral closure, model intersection weights and weighted decreasing continuity. Applied to max(phi,psi−epsilon), it gives MA(psi)({phi<psi−epsilon})≤MA(phi)({phi≤psi−epsilon}); letting epsilon decrease proves integral_{phi<psi} MA(psi)≤integral_{phi<psi} MA(phi). Use the correctly signed
I(phi,psi)=integral (phi−psi)(MA(psi)−MA(phi))≥0,
J_psi(phi)=E(psi)−E(phi)+integral (phi−psi)MA(psi),
with I/(n+1)≤J_psi≤nI/(n+1). Corollary 10.4 proves equal MA iff I=0 iff the difference is locally constant. On irreducible X, normalized potentials with I=0 agree at all divisorial points by the energy estimates tested against finite-energy divisorial Dirac masses, hence agree globally by minimal usc extension. Corollary 10.6 gives domination: for rho=max(phi,psi) equal to psi almost everywhere for MA(psi), I(rho,psi)=−integral(rho−psi)MA(rho)≤0, and separation forces equality everywhere. Neither result assumes smoothness.

The strong topology is weak convergence plus convergence of E. Its quasimetric is I on E1/R and I+|sup phi−sup psi| on E1. Proposition 12.7 gives a bi-Lipschitz MA embedding into the dual-energy measure quasimetric. Theorem 10.14 proves that target space complete before assuming envelopes. Surjectivity therefore gives I-completeness. These are the actual general-variety implications of Theorem 12.8. Its compactness reference is supplied by general Theorem 5.11 once n1 proves envelopes, not by transferring the smoothness of Theorem 12.9. The reverse implication can be checked using uniformly bounded increasing model competitors for continuous obstacles, without placing arbitrary non-E1 increasing nets into E1.

The full proof and corrected signs are in P16.1-argument.md and the standalone P16.1-paper.tex. Literal source proof bodies and application checks are in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. notes.text:
Complete result for the exact retained P16.1 domain. For every reduced irreducible geometrically unibranch projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field k, and every ample line bundle L or ample real numerical Cartier class omega, n1–n3 establish the genuine mixed finite-energy Monge–Ampère theory. The reference is zero, V=(omega^n)>0, E=((omega,phi)^(n+1))/((n+1)V), E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c, and raw diagonal mass is V. A positive Radon target nu of mass V is solvable precisely when E_dual(nu/V)<∞, equivalently every E1 potential is target-integrable. The solution is unique modulo one real constant, with sup phi=0 fixing it. Support is arbitrary subject to finite energy. Genuine normalized compactness, continuous envelopes, two-sided energy differentiation, bounded-J target integration, comparison, domination and I-completeness all hold with the smoothness uses replaced. No countability restriction or indispensable unresolved application premise remains in this source-based proof.

Normalization descent is proved beyond a set bijection. The normalization q:X^nu→X is finite birational of degree one. Geometric unibranchness makes its geometric fibers single points with purely inseparable residue extensions; characteristic zero makes those fields equal. Thus q is a universal homeomorphism and q^an a homeomorphism. Actual global psh descent follows separately from BJ Lemma 5.13 applied to omega_m=(1+1/m)omega, whose envelopes follow from n1. This gives an onto psh homeomorphism. Degree-one projection formula gives (q*omega)^n=V. Model pairing identities extended by approximation give E(q*phi)=E(phi) and correspondence of E1 spaces. BJ equation (7.18), or PL testing against the equal energy pairings, gives exact pushforward of genuine mixed measures. The analytic homeomorphism identifies target measures uniquely, and the onto E1 correspondence gives equal dual energies. Reference, volume, energy, measure and equation therefore descend without a hidden degree factor.

Singular normal example: X={xy=z²}⊂P3 with L=O_X(1), V=2. It is an integral hypersurface, hence S2, with only the singular vertex [0:0:0:1] in codimension two. Thus R1 holds and X is normal and geometrically unibranch, but nonsmooth. Every admissible mass-two target is solvable, including 2 delta_v for divisorial v.

Nonnormal unibranch example: C={y²z=x³}⊂P2 with L=O_C(1), V=3. Its normalization is q:P1→C, [u:v]↦[u²v:u³:v³]. The cusp ring k[t²,t³] lacks the integral element t. The map is finite birational of degree one, has one point in each geometric fiber and equal residue fields, and is an isomorphism away from the cusp. Thus C is geometrically unibranch despite being nonnormal. Also q*L=O_P1(3). Blow up P1×A1 at (u=0,0), with exceptional E, and use model class p*O(3)+3X0−3E. Its degrees on the strict-transform and exceptional central components are zero and three, with multiplicities one. The genuine intersection formula gives raw measure 3 delta_ord_(u=0). Its bounded continuous model potential is 3 max(1−s,0) on that ray and three on other rays. Proven normalization descent gives a genuine continuous finite-energy solution on the cusp.

Actual multibranch obstruction: on an irreducible rational nodal curve, normalization P1 has distinct p1,p2 mapping to the node. For ample L of degree d>0, v=ord_p1 is a divisorial valuation of the common function field and delta_v has finite dual energy downstairs by BJ Proposition 11.1. The blowup of P1×A1 at (p1,0), with nef model class p*(q*L)+dX0−dE, has genuine raw measure d delta_v. Its continuous potential g equals d max(1−s,0) on the p1 ray and d on other rays, giving endpoint values zero and d at p1,p2. If a downstairs E1 solution existed, normalization energy/pushforward identities and positivity would give its upstairs pullback measure d delta_v, since the analytic preimage of this valuation is a singleton. Uniqueness upstairs forces that pullback to equal g+c. A downstairs pullback must have equal values at the two endpoints mapping to the node, whereas g+c differs by d. This contradiction proves actual nonsolvability of this finite-energy target for the genuine source operator. It is not merely an obstruction to a proof strategy, nor a claim that every target on the nodal curve fails.

The conclusion solves the unchanged original singular/unibranch axis with explicitly retained field and polarization hypotheses. It does not claim arbitrary-valuation, positive-residue-characteristic, nonample or nonalgebraizable results, or solve the full seven-axis family. One-constant uniqueness is asserted for irreducible X. In the source’s general equidimensional scope component raw masses are (omega^n)_(X_alpha), and ambiguity is locally constant; disjoint components have independent constants. No stronger reducible or disconnected theorem is asserted.
